- When sentiment is negative (≤ -1.00) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- When sentiment is positive (≥ 1.00) in recent days, model often underestimates upward momentum; increase forecast slightly to capture sentiment-driven rally.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in early part of 30-day horizon (days 1–7) when sentiment is neutral or negative — apply upward bias to first 5–7 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days — reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overreaction.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model tends to overcorrect upward — dampen forecast peak by 1–3%.
- Sentiment shift from negative to neutral/positive triggers model lag — delay forecast adjustment until sentiment stabilizes (wait 2–3 days after sentiment change).
- Horizon-specific: last 5–7 days of forecast often overestimate true price — apply downward correction of 0.5–1.5% to avoid overconfidence in short-term momentum.
